title: factdiff.py anchor --file retries a fact whose only anchor row is unlocated by a failed fetch
goal: factdiff.py anchor --file re-anchors a fact of the named file whose anchor row is unlocated:fetch-error, not-text or gone, as it does a fact with no row, or kb/_self/tools.md says such a row needs --source. Found by the SP-htl7jkrm review: a planted ledger with one unlocated:fetch-error row and a fetch that now answers 200 gave 'anchor: sources=0' and no fetch (_tools/factdiff.py:633).

gates.question: How does anchor --file fetch the source of a fact whose row is unlocated:fetch-error, not-text or gone: from the document cache within --max-age, or always past it? fetch_doc caches failed answers too, so a retry inside --max-age days of the failure would read the cached error and retry nothing.
When the retry still fails, does anchor --file replace the unlocated row with the new one (new verified_utc) or keep the old row untouched?
options: replace the row, as every other selection does
keep the old row when its status is unchanged
gates.recommendation: replace the row, as every other selection does
gates.answer: replace the row, as every other selection does

notes: Premise: cmd_anchor with --file F alone and a ledger holding one unlocated:fetch-error row for the file's only fact printed 'anchor: sources=0', fetched no source and wrote nothing (run 2026-10-13 at base, planted ledger, fetch_all stubbed). Keep unlocated:no-match rows unfetched: the existing anchor_file test expects no fetch when every fact holds a row. Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 4 of 15, "Freshness and census: the down window, the confirmable rule, soft 404s, unlocated anchors and mirror licences"): a lookup returns a wrong or missing fact until it is fixed, which the held-out answer-rate fitness test of EP-gzr4mmkm reads. Test ids are near the ceiling: extend the existing anchor --file test in test_live_kb.py and append the selector words to its name, a new id only when none does.
